newsitem.title: CANADA: Bumper crop, shipping delays plug Manitoba Pool.
newsitem.headline: Bumper crop, shipping delays plug Manitoba Pool.

text.p: A bumper crop, busy export season and ship delays plugged Manitoba Pool Elevators' inland and Thunder Bay export terminals, an MPE official said.

"Right now, we're operating six days a week on one or two shifts, whatever's required for the space that's available. Normally, August and September are pretty slack months but this year it's moving out," MPE operations general manager Dennis Hunter told Reuters.
MPE handles 17 percent of grains, oilseeds and specialty crops shipped through Thunder Bay, its annual report showed.

Production of western Canada's six major grains and oilseeds, wheat, barley, canola, flax, oats and rye, was estimated at 52.8 million tonnes up 14.3 percent from 46.2 million last year, the Canadian Wheat Board said.
MPE unloaded 1.73 million tonnes of commodities in Thunder Bay in 1994/95 (Aug/July) through two terminal elevators.
One terminal was closed last year in an on-going exercise by the cooperative to pare down its costs.
"The receipts down there this year has twice as much volume through the one house than what we did in both houses last year," Hunter said.
The remaining terminal has a capacity of 170,000 tonnes and was filled with grains and oilseeds. A 25,000-tonne vessel was expected to load canola and flax by month's end, he said.
"Any diversions there, are for non- (Canadian Wheat) Board grains. Right now, we're waiting for a canola vessel," Hunter said, adding there were no delays in CWB grain shipments.
Eighty percent of Thunder Bay's volume are CWB grains.
"When we closed Pool 3 everybody said we should have kept it open but what we need is more vessels," Hunter added.
A rival firm, however, handles 14 percent of volume through a 210,040 tonne elevator.
"I understand MPE had a specific difficulty that they're trying to deal with. The port is operating at peak capacity," Pioneer Grain Co Ltd vice-president Jim Weir said.
Saskatchewan Wheat Pool operates a 240,000 tonne terminal and has a second 120,000 tonne facility it runs in peak shipping seasons.
SWP handles 35 percent of Thunder Bay's volume.

"Things got congested enough that we opened our second plant two weeks ago. We may in fact had been in the same position (as MPE) had we not had that option," SWP terminal elevators general manager Jeff Robertson said.
Volume of commodities shipped through Thunder Bay since the beginning of the new crop year was 20 percent higher than the same period in the previous year, he said.
Both Robertson and Weir said vessels arrived at their terminals on time.
Available space in Prairie elevators continued to tighten as harvest progress.
Vacancy along Canadian National Railway Co lines Monday declined to 22.9 percent while space along Canadian Pacific Ltd fell to 17.1 percent, CWB spokesman Justin Kohlman said.
"In the country, it's not much different. The last time I looked, we had, out of 125 elevators, we had about 80 of them plugged," MPE's Hunter said.
-- Gilbert Le Gras 204 947 3548
